text:
maria: Quick heads-up — did a full sweep on MI250 pools tonight. Found a pattern of missing ROCm kernels for attention paths at larger sequence lengths (>=4096).
kevin: ugh. is this the autotune table gap or missing compiled kernels in the packaging?
maria: looks like both. autotune selected fwd/bwd kernels for 1024/2048 but for 4096 it tries a tiled kernel that's not present in the ROCm build we ship. same for some kv-cache helpers.
anya: can you paste the failing callsite logs?
maria: sure — snippet from the runtime trace: 
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:05Z] model=gemma_v2 hw=mi250 seq=4096 kernel_lookup: attention_tiled_16x64 NOT_FOUND -> fallthrough
[2026-03-17T02:14:05Z] fallback: attention_generic_128x32 selected
[2026-03-17T02:14:05Z] exec: attention_generic_128x32 latency +12ms / token
```
kevin: that extra 12ms is noticeable on P99. Do we have numbers across batch sizes?
maria: yes — small table from the perf run: 
```
seq  batch=1  batch=8  batch=32
1024  6ms      3ms      2.2ms
4096  22ms     11ms     9.8ms  (with fallback)
```
jordan: can we add a conditional routing rule: if hw=mi250 and seq>=2048 and kernel_missing -> route to mi100 pool where tiled kernel exists? Risky but keeps latency stable.
sara: routing to mi100 will change cost profile (higher unit cost), and we need to ensure model determinism. Also we need a fast check in hot path; a synchronous kernel probe at request time will kill latency.
anya: proposal: maintain a cached capability matrix per node (updated by background probe during deploy/instance-start). Use that matrix in the decision path — O(1) check instead of probe. If matrix says kernel missing, trigger routing policy.
kevin: agree. we already have a small matrix for quant profiles. We can extend it to include kernel variants keyed by (arch, seq_bucket, plugin_version).
maria: example matrix we generated: 
```json
{
  "mi250": {
    "seq_bucket_0_1024": ["att_fwd_128" , "att_bwd_128"],
    "seq_bucket_1025_4096": ["att_fwd_16_tiled"],
    "seq_bucket_4097_plus": []
  },
  "mi100": {
    "seq_bucket_4097_plus": ["att_fwd_16_tiled", "att_bwd_16_tiled"]
  }
}
```
kevin: nice. two follow-ups: 1) who owns probe / updater? 2) fallback routing policy semantics (route vs degrade on host)?
jordan: runtime infra can own the probe updater — runs at start and on kernel-install events. Policy: prefer local host degrade (use generic kernel) if latency impact within SLO; otherwise route to compatible pool with a soft cap to avoid throttling another pool.
sara: need metrics in console — per-route kernel-missing counter, percent of requests rerouted, latency delta. Also add a regression alert when generic fallback is used > 2% for 5m.
ci-bot: perf artifact uploaded: https://perf.redwood.local/archives/1805123456/mi250-kernel-sweep.tar.gz
perf-bot: summary: 27 failing kernel lookups across 12 instances, median extra latency 9.5ms per token when falling back.
maria: i'll open a lightweight RFC with the matrix shape + updater design and a runtime PR that wires the cached check into the hot path (very shallow change). will add an opt-in flag `rocm.enable_kernel_matrix` behind feature-flag.
kevin: also add a small self-check endpoint `/_kernel_status` for debug (read-only) that dumps matrix for that node. don't expose it in prod without auth.
anya: i'll own the tests (unit + integration against CI images). will add a synthetic job that forces missing kernel and asserts routing decisions.
maria: timeline: draft RFC today, runtime PR by EOD tomorrow, integration tests by end of week. tagging @eng-oncall for visibility — this can cause P99 regressions if we don't ship the matrix fast. :eyes:
kevin: thanks — please link PR and RFC here once ready. :thumbsup:
